subject: Sandbox voucher rotation - triage and approval
messages:
From: Anna Perez <anna@vantage-labs.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T09:22:00Z
Subject: Request: additional sandbox credits for evaluation

Hi Hannah,

We really appreciate Redwood's responsiveness on our pilot. Our engineering teams are split across three pods and each pod started its own sandbox account to run isolated benchmarks. We ran out of the initial vouchers faster than expected and would like to request an additional set of sandbox vouchers for the remaining pods so we can finish the evaluation next week.

High-level:
- Company: Vantage Labs
- Use case: vector search + retrieval-augmented generation pipeline
- Teams: 3 pods (research, infra, integrations)
- Current ask: +50 eval credits per pod (150 total)

If you need any verification, I can share account aliases and a short list of team emails. We value Redwood's latency profile and want to complete the proof-of-concept before committing.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Perez
Head of ML, Vantage Labs
anna@vantage-labs.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-14T12:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: additional sandbox credits for evaluation

Folks — forwarding Anna's request. Ops flagged multiple voucher requests that look suspicious: same org, different emails, promo reuse. Can you run a quick triage and confirm whether this looks like legitimate team fragmentation vs. coordinated voucher rotation?

Questions to answer:
- Are the account emails tied to the same billing / company domain?
- IP / device overlap on provisioning events?
- Any evidence of promo code reuse or scripted signups?

Please attach logs and a short recommendation (deny / one-time exception / escalate to sales). I can own the external communication once we have a decision.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional sandbox credits for evaluation

Quick summary from triage (see attached session-logs-20261014.csv and screenshot):

Findings:
- We observed 6 voucher provisioning requests originating from 3 distinct emails over a 48-hour window.
- Provisioning IPs: three distinct public IPs that resolve to the same /24 range (likely same office / cloud provider).
- Promo code usage: same promo token was attempted against two accounts after it had already been redeemed once (redemption attempt logged).
- Account metadata: phone numbers and recovery emails differ, but billing contact fields show the same corporate domain (vantage-labs.com) for two of the accounts.

Interpretation:
- This looks like a mix of legitimate pod splits and attempts to chain vouchers across accounts (voucher replay attempts present). Pattern matches previous voucher-rotation cases where teams spin multiple sandboxes to extend free evaluation time.

Recommendation (pick one):
1) Deny additional free credits and offer a sales-led paid pilot with a 30% pilot credit — if they want more run-time we convert to a paid pilot.
2) Grant a single, consolidated sandbox (one account) with a one-time 7-day extension and require team consolidation and validation (list of team emails) — monitor usage and drop further free grants if reuse continues.

My leaning: option 2 as a low-friction compromise, but block any further promo token reuse by marking those accounts under investigation.

Attachments: session-logs-20261014.csv (provisioning events), screenshot-claim-1.png (promo error showing attempted reuse).

Marissa
Sr. Risk Analyst, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-15T10:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional sandbox credits for evaluation

I reviewed Marissa's logs — concur with her read. Two operational notes:
- If we go with option 2 (one-time 7-day extension), require explicit consolidation (they must pick a single account and MX-confirm the team emails). Enforce via a verification checklist.
- If we deny, provide a sales offer: 30% pilot credit (applies on first invoice) to keep the opportunity warm.

My vote: option 2 with the consolidation guardrails. Happy to have Sales (Jordan or Marissa) draft the conditional language.

Sean
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Anna Perez <anna@vantage-labs.com>
Cc: ops@vantage-labs.com
Date: 2026-10-16T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: additional sandbox credits for evaluation

Hi Anna — thanks for the patience while we reviewed your request. We ran a short operations triage and found evidence of multiple provisioning events and a reuse attempt of the same promo token across accounts. Because of that pattern, we can’t approve an open grant of additional vouchers.

That said, we want to keep the pilot moving. Two paths you can pick from:

A) One-time consolidated sandbox: we will provision a single sandbox account for Vantage Labs and grant a one-time 7-day extension (no extra voucher tokens). You must confirm the canonical account email and provide a short list of team members who will access it. We will monitor usage and revoke the extension if voucher reuse is detected.

B) Sales-led paid pilot: if you prefer continuous access, our Sales team can set up a paid pilot with a 30% pilot credit applied to the first invoice. This avoids free-credit gating and keeps your evaluation uninterrupted.

Please reply which option you prefer and include the canonical account email if you pick A. If you want help consolidating team access I can loop in our Solutions Engineering contact.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
